---
title: "check-note-sheet-rows.yml"
---

Diff-scoped check that flags a note-sheet table row
holding more than one concept.
The lab's rule (Ezra, 2026-10-22) is that a note sheet
gives each concept its own row:
one formula and one short label, with no prose.
This implements
[gha#1164](https://github.com/Morrison-Lab/gha/issues/1164).

The check reads pipe tables (`| label | formula |`)
in the files `globs` matches, by default `*note-sheet*.qmd`.
It reports a row the pull request adds when:

- the label holds notation,
  unless the label is a link to the term's definition;
- the label joins two concepts with a comma or "and";
- one cell holds two formulas joined by a comma, a semicolon or "and".

A label that ends in `, ... form`, `version` or `case`,
such as `Sample MSE, matrix form`,
names one concept in a second form, in a row of its own.
It is not flagged.
Header rows and rows inside code fences are ignored.

Two prose rules are errors whatever `fail` says,
because they are deterministic
([gha#1201](https://github.com/Morrison-Lab/gha/issues/1201)):

- a row's label is a sentence (it ends in `.`, `!` or `?`, or runs past six words),
  or a cell after the label has words outside math;
- a line outside a table is a paragraph, an inline list included.
  Headings, bold-only labels, link-only lines, div fences, table captions,
  bullets (with their indented continuation lines), images, blockquotes,
  raw HTML, HTML comments and the YAML front matter are allowed.
  Link text in a formula cell counts as words.
  Every list is a table or bullets, as on the
  [rme exam formula sheet](https://morrison-lab.github.io/rme/chapters/exam-formula-sheet.html).

The check is diff-scoped:
an added line whose exact text was also deleted
in the same diff counts as moved.
With no base ref, or when the diff cannot be computed,
it skips with a warning instead of scanning the whole tree,
unless `whole-tree` asks for that.

## Inputs

- `globs`: space-separated git pathspecs of tracked files to check
  (default `*note-sheet*.qmd`).
- `paths-ignore`: comma- or newline-separated glob patterns to skip.
- `fail`: fail the workflow on a one-concept finding
  (default `false`, warning annotations only).
  The prose rules always fail, whatever `fail` says.
- `whole-tree`: scan every matching file in full (default `false`).
- `python-version`: Python version to set up (default `3.x`).
- `runs-on`: runner label for the job (default `ubuntu-latest`).
  Use a self-hosted label only for a private repository;
  never for a public one, whose pull requests can run arbitrary code on it.

The prose rule is PSW's
"Give each concept in a note sheet its own row".
